governance.attested_by: ercot 26 gtc-limits-v1: ercot 25 chp-floor-v1 base + ercot_gtc_limits_measured, 2026-07-02
governance.note: ercot 26 = ercot 25 chp-floor-v1 (ercot 24 ct-drag-v1 base + the measured CHP steam-following export floor + de-circularized CHP benchmark) with the measured ERCOT GTC transfer-limit overlay enabled (ScenarioConfig.ercot_gtc_limits_measured) and NO new offer-curve deltas or fitted adders. The overlay replaces the static ttc_mw on the links that carry ERCOT's published Generic Transmission Constraints (PNHNDL -> Panhandle->North; WESTEX -> West->North + West->South_Central split 8:3; NE_LOB -> Northeast->North; constants.ERCOT_GTC_LINK_MAP) with the measured hourly limit series curated from the NP6-86 'SCED Shadow Prices and Binding Transmission Constraints' archive (gtc-limits clean datatype). Each hour ERCOT reported a constraint takes the mean of its enforced 5-minute limits; unobserved hours revert to the calibrated static limit-at-bind; the import direction keeps the static thermal rating (a GTC is an export stability limit, not an import rating). Rule #14 admissibility: a GTC limit is ERCOT's published voltage/WSCR stability transfer limit, a reproducible physical/market input that regenerates every year and responds to changed grid conditions; the reported HSL curtailment totals remain the validation target and are never read by the overlay. Applied only when the year has BOTH the gtc-limits partition AND measured HSL renewable potential (2023 only; 2024/2025 ride EIA-930-delivered-as-CF and are byte-identical to ercot 25, the overlay skipped to avoid double-curtailment). RESULT: the overlay is neutral on the backcast (2023 curtailment wind 2.45->2.46, solar 0.45->0.46 TWh; CC_REGULAR grid 133.18->133.19), because the West/Panhandle export interfaces carry only ~3 GW against ~10 GW of capacity and saturate <1% of hours - the missing curtailment is nodal/intra-zone (the intra-zone GTCs VALEXP/MCCAMY and sub-GTC 138 kV limits the 7-zone reduction cannot represent), not at the zonal interface. Per rule #1 the structurally-correct mechanism stays in (default off) even though the residual did not move; it is the correct foundation for a future sub-zonal/nodal representation. No unit pinned to observed CEMS generation; no adder/haircut tuned to price or volume residuals; all offer-curve deltas inherited from ercot 24 unchanged.

exceptions.reason: C1 fuel-mix CC_REGULAR 2023: model 133.19 TWh grid (135.15 incl. behind-meter) vs grid-delivered actual 141.74 (EIA-923 143.70; -8.55 TWh, share -1.6pp; band ±4.46). Root cause quantified and now CONFIRMED, not tuned (rules #1/#11): the model under-curtails 2023 renewables by ~4.1 TWh - model curtailment 2.46 TWh (wind 2.46 + solar 0.46, endogenous negative-price re-curtailment of HSL potential) vs ISO-reported 6.96 TWh (wind 4.864 + solar 2.092); the model's extra renewable energy displaces the marginal class (CC_REGULAR), which in reality served that load. The structural fix hypothesized in ercot 25 (wire measured GTC/interface limits, rule #14) was IMPLEMENTED in this run and is proven NEUTRAL: the measured hourly PNHNDL/WESTEX/NE_LOB export limits net out to the static ratings (median PNHNDL 2582 vs static 2680), and the West/Panhandle export interfaces carry only ~3 GW against ~10 GW capacity, saturating <1% of hours - so no accurate zonal limit can bottle the missing energy. ERCOT's real curtailment is nodal/intra-zone (VALEXP/Rio Grande Valley, McCamey, West/Panhandle-internal 138 kV) - constraints the 7-zone reduction cannot represent. A secondary ~3.7 TWh basis inconsistency persists: grid-delivered EIA-923 gas class actuals (205.1 TWh) exceed the EIA-930 gas grid meter (201.5) the model's demand is built from, so the per-class actuals structurally exceed any dispatch serving the 930 demand and the shortfall lands on the marginal class. The remaining honest fix is a sub-zonal/nodal topology (split West/Panhandle to expose the intra-zone pockets), a separate work stream; closing this with an offer retune or a renewable haircut fitted to the residual is forbidden. Note 2024 CC_REGULAR passes (-3.14 TWh) and 2025 is preliminary-vintage skipped, so this is a single-year residual of a mechanism otherwise in band.

C2 system volume gas 2025: -2.8% (threshold ±2.5%). Model all-gas = 194.54 TWh vs EIA-930 = 200.21 TWh (unchanged from ercot 25 - the GTC overlay is skipped for 2025, so the 2025 solve is byte-identical). The 2025 EIA-923 vintage is a preliminary monthly-survey release (9/41 CC_REGULAR, 3/19 CC_CHP, 24/38 CT_PEAKER plants missing), so there is no trustworthy per-class actual and the family falls back to the EIA-930 aggregate. The model matches the preliminary EIA-923 gas total almost exactly; the residual gap is dominated by the 930-vs-preliminary-923 vintage difference (generators on the grid meter not yet in the 923 filing). Expected to shrink as the 2025 filing matures; no fleet addition or dispatch change can close it honestly.

C3b price duration shape 2023: NRMSE ~0.327. LP dual-based prices structurally compress the price distribution relative to real-market settlement prices which carry ORDC scarcity adders, startup cost uplift, and congestion rents. Closable only with deeper energy+reserve co-optimization; per rule #1, no fitted adder applied. The GTC overlay's marginal 2023 flow changes do not materially move the duration curve. 2024 PASSES (NRMSE 0.199).

C3c price tail 2025: model 6 hours > $200 vs actual 31 (ratio 0.19, threshold [0.5, 2.0]). Byte-identical to ercot 25 (GTC overlay skipped for 2025). The co-opt ORDC demand curve produces scarcity pricing but not enough 2025 tail hours; the DAM-AS overlay starts 2024 and the 2025 tail is driven by tight-reserve afternoons the perfect-foresight LP smooths. Structural (LP-dual compression), not closable with a fitted offset.

C5c storage dispatch shape 2024: r=-0.306. Byte-identical to ercot 25 (GTC overlay skipped for 2024). EIA-930 battery series coverage is only ~19% of 2024 hours - insufficient for a stable shape correlation - and real ERCOT batteries cycle primarily for ancillary services (~85% of revenue), which the energy-arbitrage LP does not replicate hour-by-hour. Kept as an accepted limitation: the mechanism is structural (rule #1) and is not reverted for a soft-shape metric on 19%-coverage data.

C5c storage dispatch shape 2025: r=-0.879. Byte-identical to ercot 25 (GTC overlay skipped for 2025). Same structural cause as 2024: real ERCOT storage cycles for AS (~85% of battery revenue), the model cycles for energy arbitrage. The negative correlation on the 2025 series is the AS-vs-arbitrage timing mismatch, not a volume error; the endogenous storage-AS reservation (ercot_storage_as_reserve, on from 2024) prices the reservation but does not reproduce the intra-day AS dispatch shape. Structural gap, tracked for the storage-AS co-optimization work stream.
